ITERATIONS: SEATING
SHAPE
Fig 4.5
After testing out several iterations, we determined that the shape which flows along
the contours of the seat best complements the intricate pattern. This design choice
not only aligns with the organic form we aimed to create but also enhances the
tactile experience for the user.
As the contours of the surface encourage users to interact with the chair in a more
intuitive and dynamic way, the shape of the seating encourage the user to
Fig 4.1
interact with the edges as well. By choosing this shape, the fluidity of the contours
extends to the shape, making the piece look more organic.
This choice of this shape, therefore, best embodied the overall intent of the design.
4

Fig 5.1
Fig 5.2
ITERATIONS: For the legs, we opted for a clean and minimal design to create a balanced contrast with the intricate, sculptural seat. The seat itself
is rich in texture and complexity, so keeping the base visually simple prevents the overall design from feeling overwhelming. The
STOOL LEGS
iterative design process involved exploring possible aesthetics while focusing on stability, visual balance and how the legs interact
with the seating. The final design was chosen for its well-balanced composition minimal yet bold geometric structure. This striking
framework complements the organic seating design with a clean and contemporary aesthetic.
The chosen design has four legs that are tapered, reinforced by a square-shaped connection at the bottom. The contrast between
the sleek, structured legs and the fluid, sculptural seat enhances the overall composition of the chair.

PROCESS
DOCUMENTATION
Our design was first modeled in Rhino to refine the
structure and dimensions before fabrication.
We then marked and measured the required lengths
for each metal piece before proceeding with cutting.
Once cut, an automated machine was used to bend Fig 7.7 Fig 7.8
Fig 7.6 Fig 7.6 Fig 7.6
the pieces to a precise 90-degree angle, after which
we manually adjusted them to an 80-degree angle for
the final form.
Simultaneously, we began crafting the seating using a
CNC milling machine to achieve the intricate, organic
pattern with high precision.
For the metal sheet, we incorporated a design similar
to the chair seating.
As a finishing touch, the rebars were spray-painted
black for a consistent and polished finish, while the
wooden seat was coated with a clear lacquer to
enhance its natural texture

USERS' FEEDBACKS
Uncle Goh – The Fablab
"Wah, this chair damn solid, ah! The curves all so smooth, like
made by some atas designer. Sit down also shiok, just nice,
not too hard, not too soft. Last time, where got like this one?
You young people really got skill, ah—steady lah!”
Lana – An Aspiring Architect
"The Butterfly chair is an intricate and well-crafted piece of
furniture. The seat is smoothly sanded, glossy and stands as a
work of art even without being in use. The attention to detail with
careful welding, nailing and painting the rebars matte black gave
an avant-garde aesthetic to the project. Good job guys!"
Aryan – The Raccoon Lover
“The chair has a very psychedelic-looking surface to it, so it
definitely catches people’s eyes when they enter the room. It’s
quite compact and it blends well with most environments. I
would definitely purchase this chair if it were in the market, I
believe it makes any interior decor quite interesting.”
